whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Evidence Matter in Ventura County

items.title: California's Filing Window Isn't Endless
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but if a government vehicle or a road defect on a city street like Port Hueneme Road was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to explore your options can mean losing them entirely.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault for the crash, with your share of responsibility reducing rather than erasing your compensation. Our team can help make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you before you've had a chance to respond.

items.title: Skip the Recorded Statement Trap
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, sometimes before you know the full extent of your injuries. There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in California, but an early, casual-sounding statement can be used later to minimize what you're owed.

items.question: I was in a crash near Channel Islands Boulevard — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention even if you feel okay, since injuries like concussions or soft tissue damage don't always show symptoms right away. Take photos of the scene, get the other driver's insurance information, and avoid giving a recorded statement to their insurer until you've spoken with an attorney. Contact us today for a free consultation to walk through next steps.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a city-maintained road in Port Hueneme?
items.answer: Claims involving a public entity, like a poorly maintained stretch of a city street, often carry a much shorter deadline than the standard two years — sometimes just six months to file a claim. This is one of the most common ways injured people accidentally lose their right to pursue compensation, so it's worth having an attorney check this early.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our team offers free consultations, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation to see if you have a case.
